In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the context of DL-Lite, the non-logic-based approach of extracting minimal modules based on the notion of inseparableness is more efficient than the logic-based approach.

, while logic-based module extraction methods are not always able to find the smallest possible module (as the non-logic based methods), they are able to extract modules which are significantly smaller than those found by the non-logic-based ones.
, for the investigated cases, the QBF-based module extraction approach is the only one that can produce minimal modules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a general framework for extracting minimal modules from ontologies and demonstrate that it can be used to extract large and complex modules from real-life ontologies.
the combination of logic-based module extraction and QBF solvers is a promising approach to extract minimal modules from large-scale ontologies.

, by combining logic and non-logic-based techniques, we have developed a framework for extracting minimal modules from large-scale ontologies, which are more expressive than the ones used in the literature, and which can be automatically extracted using state-of-the-art QBF solving technology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
logic-based module extraction can provide a more precise and complete description of the module than non-logic-based module extraction, while still retaining its efficiency.
the proposed approach can be used as a basis for the development of a practical tool for module extraction that can be applied to ontologies of any size.
the combination of logic-based approaches with non-logic-based ones can provide a more effective way to extract modules from ontologies.
